description: Enhanced Password Reset with 15-minute token expiry, rate limiting (max 3 requests per hour per email), email notification on successful reset, and prevention of last 3 password reuse. Integrates with existing Laravel password reset flow.
steps: 1. Create config/auth.php if it doesn't exist (copy from Laravel 12 defaults). Set 'passwords' => ['users' => ['provider' => 'users', 'table' => 'password_reset_tokens', 'expire' => 15, 'throttle' => 60]]. This sets token expiry to 15 minutes.

2. Create migration 2026_10_31_000002_create_password_history_table.php with Schema::create('password_history', ...) containing: id, user_id (FK to users, indexed), password (hashed string, 255), created_at (timestamp, no updated_at). Use $table->foreign('user_id')->references('id')->on('users')->onDelete('cascade'). Add index on user_id for fast lookups.
3. Create model app/Models/PasswordHistory.php with fillable ['user_id','password'], timestamps=false (only created_at), casts ['created_at'=>'datetime']. Relationship: belongsTo(User::class).
4. Add relationship to app/Models/User.php: public function passwordHistory() { return $this->hasMany(PasswordHistory::class); }

5. Create app/Services/PasswordHistoryService.php with methods: checkPasswordReuse(User $user, string $newPassword): bool (fetches last 3 passwords via passwordHistory()->latest()->limit(3)->get(), uses Hash::check() to compare, returns true if match found), storePassword(User $user) (creates PasswordHistory record with current user password hash). This service is called before password updates.

6. Create or modify app/Http/Controllers/Auth/ForgotPasswordController.php (if doesn't exist, create it). Method sendResetLinkEmail(Request): validate email, apply rate limiting with RateLimiter::attempt('password-reset:'.$email, 3, fn()=>true, 3600) - max 3 per hour. On exceeded, return error 'Too many password reset attempts. Please try again in 1 hour.' Use Password::sendResetLink($credentials) to send email with token. Return success message.

7. Create or modify app/Http/Controllers/Auth/ResetPasswordController.php. Method reset(Request): validate token+email+password+password_confirmation, check password against last 3 via PasswordHistoryService::checkPasswordReuse(), if reused return error 'You cannot reuse any of your last 3 passwords.' Use Password::reset() to update password. On success, call PasswordHistoryService::storePassword() to record new password hash, send PasswordResetSuccessNotification to user, and redirect to login with success message.

8. Add routes to routes/web.php: Route::middleware('guest')->group: GET /forgot-password (ForgotPasswordController@showLinkRequestForm), POST /forgot-password (ForgotPasswordController@sendResetLinkEmail) named 'password.email', GET /reset-password/{token} (ResetPasswordController@showResetForm) named 'password.reset', POST /reset-password (ResetPasswordController@reset) named 'password.update'.

9. Create Blade views: resources/views/auth/forgot-password.blade.php (email input form, submit button), resources/views/auth/reset-password.blade.php (token+email hidden, new password+confirm inputs, password requirements list, submit button). Match existing auth view styles.

10. Create app/Notifications/PasswordResetSuccessNotification.php extending Notification, via(['mail']), toMail() returns MailMessage with subject 'Your password has been reset' and body 'Your Mwalimu account password was successfully changed on [timestamp]. If you did not make this change, please contact support immediately.' Include user IP and user agent in email body for security context.

11. Modify app/Http/Controllers/Auth/RegisterController.php store() method: after user creation in the OTP flow (check OtpController for final user creation), call PasswordHistoryService::storePassword() to record the initial password hash. This ensures the first password is in history.

12. Create app/Http/Requests/UpdatePasswordRequest.php form request for password updates in user settings (not reset flow, just settings change). Validate current_password, new password with Password::defaults() rules, and check reuse with PasswordHistoryService in the authorize() or prepareForValidation() method. Use in settings controller when user changes password via settings page.
acceptance_criteria: Password reset tokens expire after exactly 15 minutes from creation
Users can request password reset max 3 times per hour per email - 4th attempt within the hour returns throttle error
Users cannot set their new password to match any of their last 3 passwords
On successful password reset, user receives email notification with timestamp and device info
Password history is recorded on: user registration (initial password), password reset, password change via settings
Attempting to reuse a recent password returns clear error message before password update
config/auth.php exists with correct expire and throttle values
verification: Run php artisan migrate to create password_history table
Register a new user, check password_history table contains 1 record with hashed password
Visit /forgot-password, enter email, verify email received with reset link containing token
Click reset link, attempt to set password to the current password - verify error 'cannot reuse last 3 passwords'
Set a new password, verify redirect to login and PasswordResetSuccessNotification email received
Attempt 4 password reset requests within 1 hour for same email - verify 4th request returns throttle error
Change password via settings 2 more times (total 3 password changes), then attempt to set password to any of the last 3 - verify error appears
Wait 16 minutes after requesting a reset token, attempt to use it - verify 'token expired' error
Check storage/logs/laravel.log for any errors during reset flow
findings: Implementation completed successfully. All password reset functionality has been added including: config/auth.php with 15-minute expiry and 60-second throttle, password_history table migration, PasswordHistory model with relationship to User, PasswordHistoryService for checking reuse and storing passwords, ForgotPasswordController with rate limiting (3 per hour), ResetPasswordController with password history validation, password reset Blade views (forgot-password and reset-password) matching existing auth styling, PasswordResetSuccessNotification with IP and user agent details, initial password storage in OtpController after registration, and UpdatePasswordRequest form request for settings. Password reset routes added to web.php under guest middleware. The migration needs to be run on the production/development environment with 'php artisan migrate' to create the password_history table. Note: Due to terminal issues in this Windows environment, the migration was not executed during implementation but the migration file is syntactically correct and ready to run.
